title.zh: 货币（硬币面额与特征）公告 2023
title.en: Currency (Denominations and Characteristics of Coins) Notification 2023

completenessNote: 该法规为单篇法律文书，无分节结构；正文按官方 front 抬头逐字全录，共 2 条。

text.en:
Currency Act 1967
Currency
(Denominations and Characteristics of Coins)
Notification 2023
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act 1967, it is notified for general information that the denomination and characteristics of the coin to be issued on 14 August 2023 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

THE SCHEDULE
Description of the 100th birth anniversary of
Mr Lee Kuan Yew commemorative coin to be issued
on 14 August 2023
Denomination
$10
Metal
Aluminium Bronze
Standard Weight
13.90 g ± 0.42 g
Standard Diameter
30.00 mm ± 0.40 mm
Standard Thickness
2.90 mm ± 0.40 mm
Shape
Round
Edge
Milled
Design of Obverse
1.The coin is gold in colour.
2.The Singapore Coat of Arms is engraved in the centre of the coin with a dual latent image directly below it and above the word “SINGAPORE”. The dual latent image features Mr Lee Kuan Yew’s birth year “1923” and his 100th birth anniversary “2023”.
3.The word “SINGAPORE” appears once in each of the 4 official languages and is engraved on the coin around the Singapore Coat of Arms.
4.The words “100TH BIRTH ANNIVERSARY” and “LEE KUAN YEW” are engraved along the top and bottom circumferences of the coin, respectively, with Mr Lee Kuan Yew’s life period “1923” and “2015” on the left and right of his name, respectively.
Design of Reverse
1.The coin is gold in colour.
2.The coin features —
(a)in the foreground —
(i)a portrait of Mr Lee Kuan Yew on the right side of the coin; and
(ii)the Marina Barrage on the bottom left side of the coin, with the right part partially covered by the portrait of Mr Lee Kuan Yew; and
(b)in the background —
(i)the skyline of the Raffles Place financial district on the top, with the right part partially covered by the portrait of Mr Lee Kuan Yew; and
(ii)the Fullerton Hotel and National Gallery Singapore on the left side and right side of the coin, respectively, in front of the Raffles Place financial district skyline. The right side of the National Gallery Singapore is partially covered by the portrait of Mr Lee Kuan Yew.
3.The denomination “$10” is engraved and placed at 9 o’clock of the coin, between the Marina Barrage and Raffles Place financial district skyline.
